bodyful_reachable_closure.measured: false. The body's own DIRECT calls are all resolved (6 resolved, 0 extern_decls, 0 unresolved; reachable closure size 4), but the TRANSITIVE closure leaves the assembled module's body prefix: `<LevelArc as Deref>::deref` is itself declaration-bearing at the seam -- its own coverage row records 2 extern_decls and a derived_mir verdict of `unsupported`.
bodyful_reachable_closure.STAYS_FAIL_BY_A_FLOOR: THREE WALLS, and only the third is a floor (corrected 2026-08-26; every earlier statement here named a build item as the reason). (1) rustc has no cross-crate THIR -- `thir_body` takes a `LocalDefId`, no `thir_of_instance`: BUILD ITEM. (2) every body-producing path keys on `def_id.is_local()` -- `trust-mir-extract` early-returns on `!is_local()`: BUILD ITEM. (3) the closure ends at a declaration with no body ANYWHERE -- `Option::expect -> expect_failed -> panic_display -> panic_fmt -> panic_impl`, and `panic_impl` occurs in all of core/src/ only as doc, comment, lang attr, declaration (`unsafe extern "Rust"`, panicking.rs:67-70) and a SAFETY note, NEVER as a definition; its definition is std/src/panicking.rs:611 `#[panic_handler]` (measured 2026-08-27: a real 4-instruction body under -Zbuild-std), and the chain below it terminates at `_Unwind_RaiseException` -- `unsafe extern "C-unwind"`, unwind/src/libunwind.rs:290, a C SYMBOL with no Rust body anywhere: FLOOR (workflow wf_1c3df27b, mechanism M2). No lowering fixes (3), and it binds any body whose emitted trust-ir reaches the panic entry. CORRECTED 2026-08-27: this note used to add 'which is why the only bodies whose bodyful cell reads holds have ZERO calls' -- FALSE, and the census re-derives the truth: 1,654 of 6,431 prefix bodies hold, 53 of them with >=1 call edge, and expr::meta::ExprMeta::has_loose_bvars (entry 3658, calling 3657) holds THROUGH its call. The floor binds bodies that REACH THE PANIC ENTRY, not bodies with calls. So the criterion is unsatisfiable AS WRITTEN for panic-reaching bodies, not merely unbuilt. BOTH citations live in the TRUST repo (compiler/ and library/), which is not committed here, so the REASON is still carried by prose in this repo; what changed is that the prose now names the floor instead of a build item. The FAIL VERDICT ITSELF is committed and measured -- see `established_by`.

bodyful_or_discharged_closure.adopted_by: owner ruling 2026-08-27 (R2+R3 of workflow wf_1c3df27b's verdict): the syntactic criterion demanded a Rust body for a chain terminating at `_Unwind_RaiseException` (unsafe extern "C-unwind", unwind/src/libunwind.rs:290), a C symbol with no Rust body anywhere -- ruled a FLOOR. The semantic obligation replaces it as the completion criterion: escaping callees are discharged clause (a) reached-and-modelled with a NAMED residual, or clause (b) unreachable-and-proved by kernel-checked theorem.
bodyful_or_discharged_closure.measured: true. The walk's escaping callees for the target are exactly {6516 Option::<T>::expect, 7211 Option::<T>::as_deref}, both clause (a) (model ir_lzb_deref; residual: Option<Arc<Level>>'s None is the null niche and as_deref().expect() is load+null-check+assert -- NOT total: ir_lzb_deref_refuses_none). The panic tail below expect is clause (b): ir_lzb_panic_path_is_unreachable, DerivedProved, 0 axiom_deps. Fail-closed both directions; zero other bodies discharge.

1_consumer_perturbation_on_the_deployed_.crate_result: 185 -> 175 flip events. 22 bodies had the perturbation APPLIED (applications>0); 11 of those flipped unperturbed; 10 of the 11 stop flipping. The 11th (`mode::CleanMode::has_cubical_layer`) still flips and that is CORRECT, not a hole: its switch is `[ 2: bb1  3: bb2 ]` where bb1 and bb2 are both `const bool true; br bb4`, so rotating the target list is the identity.
